title_he: אֵין לִבִּי יֶאֱהַב זוּלָתִי גֹּאֲלִי הֶחָבִיב
review: 1:1–2 keeps the Arabic's enjambment (لَيْسَ يَهْوَى / غَيْرَ فَادِيَّ الْحَبِيب) as 'loves none / but my beloved Redeemer', with כִּי אִם doing the work of غَيْرَ in a negative clause, as Gen 39:9 does.

1:5–6 כָּל־דָּבָר אֵין־בּוֹ מָתוֹק — the Arabic كُلُّ شَيْءٍ لَيْسَ يَحْلُو مَا خَلَا الاِسْمَ الْمَجِيد is 'nothing is sweet except the glorious name'; מָתוֹק is kept as sweetness rather than 'pleasant', since the stanza is about taste and the next line names the Name.

2:6 נַחֲלַת אֲדֹנִי וְאֵין־עוֹד — the Arabic مِلْكُ رَبِّي لَا سِوَاه is 'my Lord's possession, none besides'; the Hebrew keeps מִלְכָּה as inheritance (Num 18:20, נַחֲלָה) so what is owned is also what is given, and the closing וְאֵין־עוֹד carries the Arabic's لَا سِوَاه in four syllables instead of a second relative clause.

3:8 שֵׁם אֲדֹנִי מַחְמַד נַפְשִׁי — the printed Arabic is garbled at 'يَ اسْمُ رَبِّي مُشْتَهَاي' (the vocative يَا has lost its alif and the metre is broken, as the print's line 8 does here); the sense is 'the name of my Lord is my soul's desire', which the Hebrew supplies rather than reproducing the misprint.
